title: Meeting with Tirukkotiyur Nambigal
body:
Meeting with Tirukkotiyur Nambigal

After reforming his former teacher, Yadava Prakashar, to Vaishnavism and giving him the name of Govinda Yati, Swami Ramanujar remembered his cousin Govindan, who had saved his life years ago. Govinda Yati informs Swami Ramanujar that his cousin, now known as Ulangai Kulindha Naayanaar, is serving Lord Shiva as an Advaiti at Kalahasti. Ulangai Kulindha Naayanaar used to serve Lord Shiva, who was in the form of Bana Lingam. He used to apply sandalwood paste to the lingam, perform pushpa kainkaryam, and offer aaradhanam to Lord Shiva. At Swami Ramanujar's request, Sri Saila Purna, Swami Ramanujar's uncle, reformed Ulangai Kulindha Naayanaar and introduced him to Vaishnavism, giving him the name Embaar. Embaar took his formal leave from Lord Shiva and went to Sri Rangam to stay by the side of Swami Ramanujar.
Soon, a time came when Swami Ramanujar wished to learn the three rahasyams or secrets of Sri Vaishnava Philosophy, which are :
Tirumantram or the Asthaaksharam.
The Dwaya Mantram.
The Charama Shlokam.
Swami Ramanujar traveled to Tirukkotiyur to meet Tirukkotiyur Nambigal to learn the rahasyams. When Swami Ramanujar arrived in Tirukkotiyur, he first met Tirukkotiyur Nambigal, who asked Swami Ramanujar to return the following day. Swami Ramanujar went back to Sri Rangam and returned the next day. When Swami Ramanujar met Tirukkotiyur Nambigal the next morning, he again requested Swami Ramanujar to return the next day. Tirukkotiyur Nambigal repeated the same exercise seventeen times.
Each of the seventeen times Swami Ramanujar was sent back was an indication of a real student to return after he had gained or overcome the following to gain knowledge of the rahasyams :
1. Samsara Bijam Tholaindha Pin Varum: A student must be free from worldly desires.
2. Ahankaram, Mamakaram Tholaindha pin Varum: A student must not possess any arrogance, ego, or self-centered attitude.
3. Aathma Gnanam Kidaitha pin Varum: A student must possess the knowledge of the behavior and nature of the aathma.
4. Dehaathmabhimanan Tholaindha pin Varum: Lose the impression that the body and asthma are the same.
5. Aishwarya, Aamushmiga, Kaivalyathigalil Moham Vittu Varum: Lose the attitude of wanting to cheat anyone for money.
6. Vishayantaratil Patru vitta pin Varum: Lose the attitude of seeking a second opinion concerning the Lord and His Bhagvath Vishayam.
7. Bhagavadh Vishayatil ruchi pirantha pin Varum: Find a sense of love in the Lord and His Bhagavth Vishayam.
8. Raga-Dveshathikal Tholaindha pin Varum: Realize the actions committed in anger and desire have repercussions and act accordingly.
9. Para thantriya unarva pirandha pin Varum: Realize that we are dependent on the Lord to live.
10. Sri Vaishnavatvam kai kudiya pin Varum: Realize the meaning of compassion( Sri Vaishnavathvam).
11. Sathvika parikgraham kidaitha pin Varum: Learn to realize and enjoy the nature of Sattva Gunam.
12. Bhagavatha parikgraham kidaitha pin Varum: Learn to converse with a Bhagavatha at the first meeting.
13. Bhagavath parikgraham kidaitha pin Varum: Learn upon seeing the Lord that our thoughts must not waver, and our thoughts must solely be focused on Him through immense bhakti.
14. Ananya-Seshatvam-Upayatvam kidaitha pin Varum: Learn that we as human beings are all equals, and if there is anyone that we cannot equate ourselves to, that is the Lord.
15. Ananya Prayojanatvam kidaitha pin Varum: Learn that the most tremendous boon that the Lord offers us is moksham, and we must accept it with open arms without the desire for anything else.
16. Ananya Bhogyatvam kidaitha pin Varum: Learn that performing sharanagathi beyond all the difficulties of our life will see us through to safety and ensure the Lord's grace upon us.
17. Acharyan Kidaitha Pin Varum: A student must find a capable Acharya who can guide and teach him all of the above.
18. Tirumantra Artham kai koodum: When one satisfies all of the above, the Tirumantram, Dwayam, and Charama Shlokams come into effect in one's life.

When Swami Ramanujar returned to Tirukkotiyur Nambigal for the eighteenth time, he shared the eighteen reasons with Swami Ramanujar. He said to him that he did not doubt in his mind that Swami Ramanujar possessed the above qualities. Still, he conducted this exercise because it was how Swami Ramanujar was to test his disciples before imparting to them the knowledge of the three great secrets. Tirukkotiyur Nambigal agrees to give Swami Ramanujar the insight of the rahasyams and calls him to enter a room. As Swami Ramanujar arrived, Tirukkotiyur Nambigal noticed that Swami Ramanujar was accompanied by Nadathoor Azhwan, Embaar, and Modhali Aandaan, who were Swami Ramanujar's foremost disciples. Tirukkotiyur Nambigal questions Swami Ramanujar about how his disciples entered the room with him. Swami Ramanujar then tells Tirukkotiyur Nambigal that the three of them are like the tridandam he holds and the pavithram he wears. They are inseparable for a sanyasi.
Similarly, his three disciples are inseparable from him. They had made the same journey as Swami Ramannujar had made over the past seventeen days, and they were worthy of receiving the rahasyams. Tirukkotiyur Nambigal agreed with Swami Ramanujar and provided them with the three rahasyams and their meanings. The meanings of the three rahasyams are as follows:
Ashtaaksharam: This mantram consists of the Pranavam, followed by Namo Narayanaya. The mantra and meaning for which can be found in the Vedas and interpreted in the following way :

The meaning of the mantram can be understood in the following way. Pranavam is split into a-u-m. Where a-kaaram represents Bhagavan Mahavishnu, m-kaaram represents the jeevaathma, and u-kaaram represents Mahalakshmi. Thus, after uttering the Pranavam, when Namaha is said, one must have the feeling of no self-centeredness and a sense of total unconditional surrender. Finally, when speaking the Lord's name, Narayana, the person must wholeheartedly think of the path to reach Him. Thus, the Tirumantram can be understood as the way to Sharanagati.
Dwaya Mantram: This mantram consists of two halves—the first half acts as a means to ask the Lord and Mahalakshmi to accept our Sharanagati. The second half serves as a means to ask the Lord and Mahalakshmi to shower their grace upon us constantly.
Charama Shlokam: This shloka is the means to Prapatti as given by Lord Krishna to Arjuna, wherein Lord Krishna tells Arjuna that He is the Ultimate Truth. He tells Arjuna to surrender and put all of his faith solely in Him, and he would relieve him from the cycle of birth and death and offer moksham.

Tirukkotiyur Nambigal explains the rahasyams and their meanings to Swami Ramanujar, informing him that he is to propagate this knowledge only to disciples who possess the eighteen qualities that he had previously mentioned to Swami Ramanujar. Swami Ramanujar steps out of the closed quarters of Tirukkotiyur Nambigal and briefly thinks for a while, and decides that he must do something before leaving Tirukkotiyur. Swami Ramanujar races up to the top of the Ashtanga Vimanam of the Sowmya Narayana Perumal Temple. He tells everyone who wishes to listen that if they want to be relieved from the cycle of life and death, they must perform Sharanagati under the guidance of an Acharya. A few people who heard Swami Ramanujar asked him what the means of obtaining this divine gift was. Swami Ramanujar instructed them to seek his refuge, and he would perform the panchasamskaaram and reveal the heavenly secrets to achieve moksha. After saying this, he started to descend from the Vimanam. In this brief moment, as Swami Ramanujar descended from the Vimanam, word reached Tirukkotiyur Nambigal of what Swami Ramanujar had done in revealing the divine secrets to the general public. Tirukkotiyur Nambigal, in a fury, rushed to the temple and confronted Swami Ramanujar, saying he had betrayed his guru by revealing the divine secrets. As punishment, he would undoubtedly go to hell for treason. Swami Ramanujar prostrated himself before his guru and told Tirukkotiyur Nambigal that he was more than ready to go to hell if he could provide the means for so many people to go to Vaikuntham.
